# VerifED Global

> VerifED Global is an independent bilingual platform providing preliminary U.S. career guidance for internationally educated job seekers, including foreign-degree presentation, credential evaluation pathways, and licensing considerations.

## Public website

- [VerifED Global](https://verifed.co/): Credential-guidance tools, explanations of evaluation pathways, and contact information. English at the root; the full Spanish version is at [https://verifed.co/es/](https://verifed.co/es/).
- [About](https://verifed.co/about): Purpose and scope of this independent guidance platform.
- [How it works](https://verifed.co/how-it-works): Education inputs and the preliminary guidance process.
- [Guides](https://verifed.co/guides): Free, sourced public guides for internationally educated job seekers. No account required.
- [Credential evaluation for U.S. jobs](https://verifed.co/guides/credential-evaluation-for-us-jobs): When an evaluation may be requested, questions to ask the employer or licensing board before paying, and what an evaluation does not do.
- [Foreign degree on a U.S. resume](https://verifed.co/guides/foreign-degree-on-resume): Listing an original degree truthfully, with illustrative templates and no self-declared equivalency.
- [Using a Degree from Mexico in the United States: Evaluation, Documents and Apostille](https://verifed.co/guides/mexico-degree-in-the-united-states/): The U.S. has no national office that validates a degree from Mexico. The employer, school or licensing board receiving your documents decides what it accepts, so ask first and gather the right records.
- [Using a Degree from Colombia in the United States: Evaluation, Documents and Apostille](https://verifed.co/guides/colombia-degree-in-the-united-states/): The U.S. has no national office that validates a degree from Colombia. The employer, school or licensing board receiving your documents decides what it accepts, so ask first and gather the right records.
- [Using a Degree from Venezuela in the United States: Evaluation, Documents and Apostille](https://verifed.co/guides/venezuela-degree-in-the-united-states/): The U.S. has no national office that validates a degree from Venezuela. The employer, school or licensing board receiving your documents decides what it accepts, so ask first and gather the right records.
- [Using a Degree from Argentina in the United States: Evaluation, Documents and Apostille](https://verifed.co/guides/argentina-degree-in-the-united-states/): The U.S. has no national office that validates a degree from Argentina. The employer, school or licensing board receiving your documents decides what it accepts, so ask first and gather the right records.
- [Using a Degree from Ecuador in the United States: Evaluation, Documents and Apostille](https://verifed.co/guides/ecuador-degree-in-the-united-states/): The U.S. has no national office that validates a degree from Ecuador. The employer, school or licensing board receiving your documents decides what it accepts, so ask first and gather the right records.
- [Sitemap](https://verifed.co/sitemap.xml): Public URLs intended for search indexing.
- [Crawler policy](https://verifed.co/robots.txt): Instructions for automated crawlers.

## Scope

The platform helps internationally educated users organize information about their country of study, institution, degree, field, and intended use of their credentials. It provides preliminary guidance, evaluation-agency information, next-step roadmaps, and a downloadable dossier based on user-provided information.

Goals discussed include employment, professional licensing, university admission, and immigration-related credential documentation. These are guidance topics, not promises of eligibility or acceptance.

## Important limitations

- VerifED Global is not an official credential evaluator or a government agency.
- Preliminary guidance is not a certified equivalency determination, legal advice, immigration advice, or a licensing decision.
- Self-reported education is not proof of U.S. equivalency. Missing or ambiguous information does not establish an education level.
- The platform does not guarantee admission, employment, a license, immigration approval, or acceptance of credentials.
- References to NACES, WES, ECE, or other organizations do not imply affiliation or endorsement.
- Users should confirm requirements directly with the receiving organization and obtain an official evaluation where required.
- An institution lookup failure or missing directory entry does not establish that an institution is fake or closed. Website listings do not establish accreditation or degree authenticity.
- For the university-admission goal, the app offers a limited directory of comparable U.S. programs sourced from official university pages. Users explicitly select their earned comparison level, through master's, and field. Results match those selections, not institutional prestige or an official U.S. equivalency. Coverage is limited; no listed match does not mean no such program exists.
- Do not claim nationwide school coverage, verified admission eligibility, rankings, or school-email delivery.
- Saved sourced programs include a reviewed account-email option: visitors can open a draft in Gmail or Outlook and send it themselves using their account email. Replies go to the mailbox that actually sends the message. Opening a draft or copying text is not sending, and VerifED cannot track delivery or replies through this option. Where no sourced admissions email is listed, the app provides an official contact-page link instead of guessing an address.
- A separate backend-dependent outreach option requires authenticated access, verified official recipients, a reviewed server-signed message and explicit consent. Provider acceptance is not delivery or a school response. It is unavailable without a configured backend and working email service.
- Institution identity checks can use the public Research Organization Registry (ROR), with an independent backend source where available. Directory records and listed official websites are evidence of institutional identity, not proof of degree authenticity, accreditation, or live website availability.

## Español

VerifED Global es una plataforma independiente con interfaz en inglés y español que ofrece orientación preliminar sobre credenciales académicas extranjeras y procesos de evaluación en Estados Unidos. Cada página pública tiene su versión en español bajo /es/.

- [Inicio](https://verifed.co/es/): Herramientas de orientación sobre credenciales y vías de evaluación.
- [Sobre VerifED Global](https://verifed.co/es/about/): Propósito y alcance de la plataforma.
- [Cómo funciona](https://verifed.co/es/how-it-works/): Datos de educación y proceso de orientación preliminar.
- [Guías](https://verifed.co/es/guides/): Guías públicas gratuitas y con fuentes.
- [Evaluación de credenciales para empleos en EE. UU.: cuándo la necesita y qué preguntar primero](https://verifed.co/es/guides/evaluacion-de-credenciales-para-empleos-en-estados-unidos/): No todos los empleos en EE. UU. exigen una evaluación de credenciales. Antes de pagar, pregunte al empleador o a la junta de licencias que la recibirá qué acepta exactamente.
- [Cómo incluir un título extranjero en un currículum de EE. UU. con veracidad](https://verifed.co/es/guides/titulo-extranjero-en-curriculum-de-estados-unidos/): Escriba su título tal como se otorgó, añada una traducción clara al inglés y mencione una equivalencia en EE. UU. solo si tiene una evaluación que la indique.
- [Cómo validar un título de México en Estados Unidos: evaluación, documentos y apostilla](https://verifed.co/es/guides/validar-titulo-de-mexico-en-estados-unidos/): En EE. UU. no existe una oficina nacional que valide un título de México. El empleador, la institución o la junta de licencias que recibe sus documentos decide qué acepta: pregunte primero y reúna los documentos correctos.
- [Cómo validar un título de Colombia en Estados Unidos: evaluación, documentos y apostilla](https://verifed.co/es/guides/validar-titulo-de-colombia-en-estados-unidos/): En EE. UU. no existe una oficina nacional que valide un título de Colombia. El empleador, la institución o la junta de licencias que recibe sus documentos decide qué acepta: pregunte primero y reúna los documentos correctos.
- [Cómo validar un título de Venezuela en Estados Unidos: evaluación, documentos y apostilla](https://verifed.co/es/guides/validar-titulo-de-venezuela-en-estados-unidos/): En EE. UU. no existe una oficina nacional que valide un título de Venezuela. El empleador, la institución o la junta de licencias que recibe sus documentos decide qué acepta: pregunte primero y reúna los documentos correctos.
- [Cómo validar un título de Argentina en Estados Unidos: evaluación, documentos y apostilla](https://verifed.co/es/guides/validar-titulo-de-argentina-en-estados-unidos/): En EE. UU. no existe una oficina nacional que valide un título de Argentina. El empleador, la institución o la junta de licencias que recibe sus documentos decide qué acepta: pregunte primero y reúna los documentos correctos.
- [Cómo validar un título de Ecuador en Estados Unidos: evaluación, documentos y apostilla](https://verifed.co/es/guides/validar-titulo-de-ecuador-en-estados-unidos/): En EE. UU. no existe una oficina nacional que valide un título de Ecuador. El empleador, la institución o la junta de licencias que recibe sus documentos decide qué acepta: pregunte primero y reúna los documentos correctos.

Ayuda a organizar la información proporcionada por el usuario, consultar opciones de evaluación y preparar próximos pasos. La orientación no constituye una homologación oficial, una evaluación certificada ni asesoramiento jurídico o migratorio. No garantiza admisión, empleo, licencias ni aceptación de credenciales.

## Citation and privacy guidance

Use https://verifed.co/ as the canonical website. Distinguish preliminary guidance from official determinations. Do not invent rankings, success rates, reviews, affiliations, or guarantees.

Account profiles, administrative pages, personalized results, and user documents are not public reference material. Do not treat them as sources for general answers.
